questions.question: What should you use a trolley valve for?

options.text: Use it only to test trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it only to test trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: A trolley valve (also called a trailer hand valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release air pressure from the brake system and cause the brakes to release.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of looseness varies by engine, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Do not back up in a straight line.
Do not fix drift until you are very far off course.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should NOT be parked:
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building (except for brief stops needed for vehicle operation like refueling). Never park within 5 feet of the road edge.

questions.question: What can affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: While driving a commercial vehicle, what is allowed with text messages?

options.text: You cannot write texts, but you can read them.
You can write texts, but you cannot read them.
You cannot write or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot write or read texts.
questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving a commercial vehicle. Texting means typing or reading text on an electronic device.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does it mean?

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, where should cargo be placed in a trailer?
questions.explanation: A top-heavy vehicle is more likely to roll over. Place cargo weight as low as possible in the trailer to reduce this risk.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), shown by a yellow warning light. For older trailers, check underneath for wires from the wheel speed sensors connected to the brakes.

questions.question: Liquid surge happens in:

options.text: Tanks that have not been used for a long time.

questions.explanation: Liquid surge happens when liquid moves inside partially-filled tanks.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: How should an exhaust system be?
questions.explanation: All parts of the exhaust system must be fastened securely. Parts should not be loose, broken, or rubbing against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand to keep the other hand free
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands
At the base of the wheel

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What should you do if you suspect a leak in radioactive material cargo?

options.text: Go to the local fire department
Pick up any loose pieces of radioactive material
Continue carrying the cargo while avoiding the affected areas
Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned
questions.explanation: If you suspect a leak in radioactive material, tell your dispatcher right away. Do not touch the material. Do not use the vehicle until it has been cleaned or checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Apply your brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply your brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements very small when using this method.

questions.question: The most important reason to do a pre-trip inspection is that it helps ensure safety.
questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection ensures your safety and the safety of others on the road.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when it first begins to rain?

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway
The water has nowhere to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway
questions.explanation: When it first rains, water mixes with oil drippings on the road that have not yet washed away. This creates a slippery surface.

questions.question: What does a maximum safe speed sign mean?

options.text: It is just a suggestion; vehicles may travel faster
It applies only to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds
No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed
questions.explanation: You must never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: What should you do about tires of different sizes?

options.text: Use them only on a front axle
Use them only on a trailer's axles

questions.explanation: All tires on a vehicle should be the same size. Check that your tires match when inspecting your vehicle.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you should be able to see about how far ahead?
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.
